In mathematics, the '''Besicovitch inequality''' is a [[Geometry|geometric inequality]] relating volume of a set and distances between certain subsets of its boundary. The inequality was first formulated by [[Abram Besicovitch]].<ref>A. S. Besicovitch, On two problems of Loewner, J. London Math. Soc. 27 (1952) 141–144. </ref>

== Definition ==
Consider the n-dimensional cube <math>[0,1]^n</math> with a [[Riemannian geometry|Riemannian]] metric <math>g</math>. Let 
{{center|<math>d_i= dist_g(\{x_i=0\}, \{x_i=1\})</math>}}
denote the distance between opposite faces of the cube. The Besicovitch inequality asserts that 
{{center|<math>\prod_i d_i \leq Vol([0,1]^n,g)</math>}}
The inequality can be generalized in the following way. Given an n-dimensional [[Riemannian manifold]] M with connected boundary and a smooth map <math>f: M \rightarrow [0,1]^n</math>, such that the restriction of f to the boundary of M is a [[degree of a map|degree]] 1 map onto <math> \partial [0,1]^n</math>, define 
{{center|<math>d_i= dist_M(f^{-1}(\{x_i=0\}), f^{-1}(\{x_i=1\}))</math>}} 
Then <math>\prod_i d_i \leq Vol(M)</math>.

The Besicovitch inequality was used to prove [[systolic geometry|systolic inequalities]]
on surfaces.<ref>[[Mikhael Gromov (mathematician)|Mikhael Gromov]]. ''Filling Riemannian manifolds.'' J. Differential Geom. 18 (1983), no. 1, 1-147. {{doi|10.4310/jdg/1214509283}} </ref><ref>P. Papasoglu, Cheeger constants of surfaces and isoperimetric inequalities, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 361 (2009) 5139–5162.</ref>
